Exact inconsistencies found

Location Exact/conflicting statement (summary) Why inconsistent Correction
docs/CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md §2.4 / MELIRA description (around line 112) "MELIRA menggunakan Large Language Model (LLM) eksternal maupun model lokal yang dapat dikonfigurasi sesuai kebutuhan pengguna." Presented local models as a supported/configurable deployment option, conflicting with established decision: external AI SaaS providers only, no local LLM inference/local AI compute/local GPU in CARES deployment model. Replaced with statement that MELIRA uses explicitly selected/configured external AI SaaS providers; local LLM inference, local models, and local GPU infrastructure are not part of the CARES deployment model.
docs/CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md §13.1 AI Provider Management (around lines 799–808) Provider list included Ollama and listed Custom API endpoint without external-only/non-local qualification in a context that followed local-model wording. Ollama is a local-model/runtime option and implied locally hosted AI as supported; provider section did not clearly exclude local inference/local GPU or restate no silent failover. Removed Ollama; reframed providers as supported/explicitly configured external AI SaaS providers (subject to approval) and limited custom endpoint to explicitly approved external compatible API endpoints meeting transport/egress/privacy/security policy; added explicit exclusion of local inference/local models/self-hosted runtimes/local GPU and prohibition on silent failover.
docs/CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md §20 "Arsitektur Pengembangan" technology table (around lines 1209–1221) `Backend Go / Python` Presented Go and Python as equally open backend candidates, conflicting with established CARES backend decision (Python primary/established backend).
docs/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md baseline and Phase 0 presentation (lines 5, 23, 60, 64) Baseline text stated "original Phase 0 through Phase 10 assignments..." while CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md defines the original approved product roadmap as Phase 1–Phase 10 (ten product-development phases). Roadmap introduced Revised Phase 0 but did not explicitly distinguish it from the ten original product-development phases. Inconsistent Phase 0–10 vs Phase 1–10 presentation and risk of implying Phase 0 is part of the original ten-phase product roadmap. Clarified baseline as the approved original product roadmap of ten product-development phases (Phase 1 through Phase 10); marked Revised Phase 0 as a proposed preparatory/documentation stage outside the ten original product-development phases; explicitly stated it must not alter original Phase 1–10 scope/numbering/assignments and that no additional authoritative Phase 0 product-definition is invented.

  • docs/CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md
  • docs/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md

Decisions preserved

  • AI deployment model: MELIRA uses external AI SaaS providers only; local LLM inference/local AI compute are not part of CARES deployment; no local GPU infrastructure required for AI inference; customers may explicitly select supported/configured external providers/endpoints as approved by policy; CARES must never silently fail over to another provider/model/region/endpoint; CARES core functionality must remain operational when MELIRA is unavailable or disabled.
  • Backend technology: Python remains the established CARES backend decision. No new technology decision introduced. Legitimate component-specific references preserved (e.g. endpoint agent/component evaluations in other documents).
  • Roadmap: Original ten-phase product roadmap (Phase 1–Phase 10 in CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md) preserved; no phases added, removed, merged, reordered, or reassigned in the approved original roadmap; no established phase scope changed.
  • Governance/integrity: All established CARES technical and commercial constraints preserved; no owner-level decisions changed or invented; ADR statuses unchanged; no proposed controls marked implemented; no security validation or production readiness claimed.

Ambiguities not resolved

  • Phase 0 authority/scope: Revised/proposed Phase 0 is treated in docs/DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md as a proposed preparatory/documentation stage. This alignment explicitly distinguishes it from the original ten Phase 1–10 product-development phases but does not invent an authoritative original Phase 0 product-definition. If future documents introduce Phase 0 terminology, they must preserve this distinction unless owner/architecture governance explicitly defines and approves otherwise.
  • Provider support/approval details: Supported external AI SaaS provider list, custom external compatible endpoint approval criteria, data-class/region/retention/training/consent/budget policies remain owner/privacy/legal/security decisions; documentation states eligibility/constraints only.
  • Historical sequencing language: Non-baseline historical/proposal/review documents may contain revised-sequencing or phase-mapping language in their original context. These were not rewritten except where targeted inconsistencies were identified; their historical rationale is preserved and should be interpreted together with the clarified baseline in CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md and DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md.

Cross-document verification (source Markdown, excluding generated dist/ export)

Searches performed after corrections:

  • Local LLM / Ollama / model lokal as supported options: no remaining Ollama or "local model/LLM as supported deployment option" statements found. Remaining matches for local inference/local GPU/local model in source docs are prohibitions, exclusions, rejected alternatives, or clarified "not part of deployment" statements consistent with the external-SaaS-only decision (including docs/adr/0004-external-ai-provider-boundary.md rejecting local model inference/local GPU service).
  • External AI SaaS: references remain present and consistent with external-SaaS-only/no local inference/no local GPU/no silent failover decisions in authoritative and aligned documents.
  • Go as backend / Go-Python backend candidates: no remaining Go / Python, "Go and Python" as equally open backend candidates, or "Go as CARES backend" candidate phrasing found in source docs. docs/TECHNOLOGY_SELECTION.md retains "Go could be efficient but violates the primary-backend language decision" (consistent with established Python backend) and endpoint-agent/component references where applicable (not CARES backend).
  • Python as backend: references remain present and consistent with the established Python backend decision.
  • Phase 0 / Phase 1–10: CARES_PRODUCT_VISION.md remains the original ten-phase product roadmap (Phase 1–Phase 10). DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md now explicitly distinguishes revised/preparatory Phase 0 from the ten original product-development phases and preserves original Phase 1–10 baseline/scope. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md does not define conflicting roadmap numbering. Source-wide verification found no Phase 0 references outside DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md and this changelog.
